records.description: The contract concerns the appointment of a service provider for the further roll-out, upgrading and updating of the current marketing automation tool, including the supply of licences. Purpose of the contract: With marketing automation, we want to do more than send emails and manage lists. We want to build relevant, honest and useful relationships with our target audiences: from international business partners to the general public. HubSpot is the current platform, but we want to take a critical look at how we use it today and how we can use it even more intelligently in the years ahead. What are we asking for? We are looking for a partner who will both think alongside us and dare to challenge us. Specifically, this involves: 1. Critical analysis of the current set-up: o Review of flows, templates, lists, naming conventions and the connection to Microsoft Dynamics 365 CRM. o Recommendations to make our set-up more efficient and impactful. 2. Developing a long-term roadmap (8 years): o Jointly determining the steps we will take to continue growing in marketing automation. o Taking account of future trends, internal needs and scalability. 3. Operational and strategic support: o Advising on and helping implement improvements, including the use of HubSpot as a press platform, lead processes and communication flows. o Support with both day-to-day operational tasks and strategic questions. o Support and advice in further embedding the use of automation tactics in our campaign activities. 4. Change management and knowledge transfer: o Taking the communications and marketing team through new working methods. o Sharing best practices to increase internal digital maturity. 5. Licence management: o Purchasing and managing HubSpot licences on behalf of PoAB, including advice on the optimal licence configuration. What do we want to achieve? • More relevant and more personal communication: so that our target audiences receive the right information at the right time. • Greater brand awareness and support: among both international and national business audiences and the general public. • A future-proof marketing organisation: with a mature marketing automation approach that is ready for the next 8 years.

records.description: Berufsgenossenschaft Verkehrswirtschaft Post-Logistik Telekommunikation (hereafter “BG Verkehr” or “the Contracting Authority”) is the statutory accident insurer for the transport, postal logistics and telecommunications sectors. It insures around 1,7 million people throughout Germany. It advises its more than 200.000 member companies on prevention and arranges treatment, rehabilitation and compensation for its insured members following accidents at work and occupational illnesses. To fulfil its prevention remit, BG Verkehr provides a wide range of publications produced both internally and externally for its affiliated sectors. The aim and subject of the contract is a “media centre” for all printed publications, physical data carriers and digital publications, with the option to order them and/or view and download them directly; ordering is generally reserved for BG Verkehr member companies. The media centre must be implemented using a modern online shop solution and operate as a standalone platform alongside the BG Verkehr website. The media centre must therefore be hosted on its own server. The services to be provided by the Contractor comprise the provision, initial customisation and commissioning (initial services), followed by operation and hosting, of a cloud-based online shop solution (media centre), including associated service, maintenance, support, training and other services. The Contracting Authority requires a market-proven, stable, secure and up-to-date shop system that is actively used and has a correspondingly large number of (agency) partners/service providers. Dependency on a single provider must not arise. If required, it must be possible to change service provider without having to change the shop system. The Contractor must use an existing shop system — or a combination of selected solutions — (for example, market-proven standard software), adapt/customise it to BG Verkehr's needs and, where necessary, develop it further. The Contractor must make the online shop solution covered by the contract available to the Contracting Authority as a cloud-based application. In doing so, the Contractor must pay particular attention to the specific accessibility requirements (see section 1.3.14), compliance with data protection requirements and requirements for data exchange through extensive interfaces, for example to the website, accounting software, inventory management system or CRM software. Subject to the provision in 13.2.2 of the EVB-IT Cloud-AGB, the EVB-IT contract for cloud services ends no later than 72 months after contract award, without notice of termination being required. Details of the terms of the individual contractual services and the options for terminating them are set out in the EVB-IT contract for cloud services (Part B.2), in particular section 3.1.

records.description: The subject of this procurement procedure is the acquisition of a software solution for the new specialist application for the future financial social welfare administration and financial asylum administration of Landratsamt Starnberg. The specialist application must enable seamless end-to-end processing of all benefits under SGB XII and the Asylum Seekers' Benefits Act (AsylbLG), as well as the processing of BuT applications. The specialist application must support fully process-oriented case handling that represents every procedural step in a structured, traceable and efficient manner. The aim is to support the handling of complex social welfare law cases (for example, under SGB XII and AsylbLG) through clearly guided user interaction, transparent status displays and intelligent automation. The focus is on process-oriented case handling based on workflows that can flexibly represent both standardised procedures (for example, receipt of applications, preparation of decisions and consultation procedures) and individual processing steps. The solution must relieve caseworkers' workload, shorten processing times and at the same time ensure compliance with legal requirements and internal review steps. In addition, traffic-light and status functions, parallel case handling, structured navigation between screens and follow-up management should contribute to a significant improvement in specialist and organisational processes.

records.description: Skatteforvaltningen (SKTFV) currently uses a case management system (SKAT Ligning) to administer SKTFV's statutory tasks, including digital processing of tax, duty and VAT checks for individuals, companies and associations. Approximately 500.000 cases are processed annually in the current SKAT Ligning, and approximately 500.000 letters are sent from SKAT Ligning (digital and physical post) each year. The current system (SKAT Ligning) no longer meets SKTFV's needs. The purpose of the tender is therefore to acquire and implement a new case management system that will gradually replace the current system. The phase-out will take place progressively through a series of projects (P1-Pn), in which users' case processing moves to the new system; the first project, which is part of the Delivery, covers the Forskud user group (P1). The new system must support SKTFV's processing of cases and the storage and structured documentation of case histories. The system must support workflows, reminders, approval flows, deadline management and role-based access control. In addition, the system must handle large volumes of letters (physical and digital) based on templates, with automatic registration in the case record. The user interface must be accessible to both administrative users and caseworkers. The system must be scalable and usable in different organisational contexts. The system must meet non-functional requirements, including performance, response times, data integrity, security, web accessibility and scalability under increased load. Management reporting must also be supported. The system must also integrate with SKTFV's existing systems and other relevant systems. It must operate on the Supplier's platform with high stability and compliance with defined service targets. Furthermore, the system's workflows must be configurable so that SKTFV can adapt the system itself after takeover. The system must support approximately 3.000 caseworkers in SKTST and approximately 120 caseworkers in VURDST. In addition, there are approximately 2.000 employees across SKTFV's other specialist agencies. SKTFV also has particular functional needs that the system must support, including display modules, management of groups of related cases, template-based letter generation, and simulation and adjustment of tax assessment bases in SKTFV's other systems — see Annex 5.a.i for a more detailed description. The system must operate on the Supplier's platform. The operating platform must be established as part of the Delivery and must be expandable as subsequent projects are implemented (Configuration Projects, cf. Annex 5.a.). The tender therefore covers the following services, cf. the Contract: • The Delivery: supply, implementation and establishment of the system (application and platform), and set-up and configuration of the Forskud user group (P1), including establishment of selected integrations with other specialist systems, including central systems such as CSR-L (SLUT), DIAS, MitID, Digital Post and the Customer's letter distributor. • Ongoing services: operation, support and maintenance of the system (application and platform). • Services on request: further development, consultancy and configuration projects for other user groups (Pn), including additional integrations with relevant specialist systems. • Cross-cutting services.
